recognize_zh: 淋巴結副皮質區有許多細胞質豐富淡粉紅、核有凹溝或折痕的組織球／樹突細胞，其間散布吞噬大量棕黑色色素的巨噬細胞（melanophages），是皮膚病性淋巴結病的典型組合。
features: Paracortex expanded by cells with abundant pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and indistinct borders
Histiocytic/dendritic nuclei that are oval, folded or grooved with fine chromatin
Macrophages laden with coarse brown-black pigment (melanin), concentrated in the upper field
Admixed small mature lymphocytes and occasional plasma cells
No sheets of atypical large lymphoid cells
describe_en: Lymph node section shows a paracortex expanded by numerous cells with abundant pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and oval, folded or grooved nuclei, consistent with Langerhans cells and interdigitating dendritic cells. Scattered and clustered macrophages contain coarse brown-black pigment, most compatible with melanin. A background of small mature lymphocytes is present, without sheets of atypical lymphoid cells. Findings are consistent with dermatopathic lymphadenopathy; a Fontana-Masson stain can confirm melanin, and clonality studies are advised if mycosis fungoides is suspected clinically.

ddx.vs: LCH shows sinusoidal sheets of grooved Langerhans cells with numerous eosinophils and necrosis, typically without melanin-laden macrophages.
Melanoma cells are cohesive, atypical and have prominent nucleoli, and the pigment lies within tumor cells that are HMB-45/Melan-A positive rather than in bland macrophages.
MF involvement shows clusters of atypical cerebriform lymphocytes and a clonal TCR rearrangement, which morphology at this power cannot fully exclude.
Hemosiderin is golden-brown and refractile and Prussian blue positive, whereas melanin is brown-black and Fontana-Masson positive.
